prize_parts.citation: For the development of palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: I keep B055 as my preferred configuration. Round 1 did not weaken the core of the case: Pd-catalysed C-N coupling is the one shortlisted achievement that is a general method for making bonds, and its impact can be counted in the synthetic literature and in process chemistry rather than projected. The chemical novelty is real. Amine binding, deprotonation and C-N reductive elimination required new ligand classes and a different mechanistic solution from the C-C couplings recognised in 2010, which is why the field matured two decades later. Thirty years of independent confirmation leave no maturity risk, and Buchwald and Hartwig, who independently established the general catalytic reaction in 1994-1995 and then drove ligand design, give a clean two-name attribution that needs no narrow carve-out of neighbouring work. I have not changed my preferred configuration after reading the other seven statements, because the objections raised against B055 (the 2010 overlap and Kosugi) were already in my round-1 case and no new argument was added. I have changed my view on how firmly to hold it against B011, as explained in the responses and uncertainties.
statement.case_against: B055 may be seen as a continuation of a field already honoured in 2010, and the chair's observation stands that it had the thinnest opening support, so it may not reach five votes whatever its merits. Kosugi's tin-amide work is a genuine antecedent, and a committee that weighs priority strictly could want him in a three-name configuration. Round 1 also showed that four members regard B011 as a new principle with consequences for what chemists and clinicians can attempt, a stronger claim of novelty than mine, and my own colleagues for B011 name the same reservation I do: no approved degrader yet. That reservation counts against them, but it does not make C-N coupling the more novel of the two.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, now holds B011 (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli) as the strongest case on the shortlist, on the grounds of a simple principle, a quantitative ternary-complex design rule, wide reproduction and late-stage clinical candidates, and he accepts that Sakamoto, Kim, Handa, Ito and Gray must be left out and defended openly.
responses.response: The ternary-complex cooperativity argument is the part of B011 that persuades me chemically, and Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands are what turn the concept into design rather than screening. My difficulty is the sentence that the omissions have to be defended openly. Any citation that says protein degradation will be read as covering both the PROTAC and the glue strands, and a trio chosen from one strand leaves the other without a citation. B055 does not have that problem, since its two names cover the full achievement. I also note that late-stage trials are not approval, and the chair's own question about what evidence would move colleagues applies to B011 as much as to my case. I will not claim that B055 is more important than B011, only that it is more complete and more settled.

responses.point: Chabes keeps Handa in the trio with Crews and Deshaies so that the cereblon identification, the chemical-mechanistic anchor of the molecular-glue branch, is covered, and words the citation to include thalidomide-class glues.
responses.response: This is the more internally consistent B011 configuration, because cereblon explains why thalidomide-class drugs work and is a chemical mechanism, not only a design idea. But it drops Ciulli, whose work gave the rational design rules that Aili, Aqvist and Linke rely on, so the two B011 groups each concede that the other trio omits something central. If I vote for B011 as a fallback I would take Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli with a PROTAC-only citation worded as such, since it is the narrower claim and the one that can be defended against the omission of Handa. I do not think the committee can resolve this dispute by deciding the glue strand is simply a footnote, and I regard that unresolved split as the strongest argument that B011 is not yet ready for a clean three-name citation.

responses.point: Brzezinski prefers B058 (Gray and Winkler) as a mature, physically stated mechanism, but concedes that priority overlaps with Marcus, Dutton and Moser, Beratan and Onuchic, and Hopfield, and that his field's proximity may inflate his view.
responses.response: I respect the maturity argument, which is the same one I make for B055, and I agree that four decades of confirmation count heavily. The difference for me is attribution. For B058 you must draw a citation narrowly around experimental demonstration in proteins to avoid overlap with a theory prize and with Dutton and Moser's distance relation, whereas the B055 priority question is limited to one precursor, Kosugi, whose reaction was stoichiometric in tin and not a general catalytic amination. The B058 case rests on a distinction between demonstrating and predicting that I find real but fine, and I doubt it can reach five votes. On your question about Kosugi in my own case, I continue to credit only Buchwald and Hartwig.

responses.point: Zou prefers B005 (Grätzel and O'Regan) as a mature, original cell architecture with clear two-person credit, and describes recognition as overdue, while acknowledging that perovskites have overtaken it commercially and that Hagfeldt may need to be added.
responses.response: We use the same test of mature validation, a sharp original discovery, and a short laureate list, and B005 and B055 are the two shortlisted items that pass it most cleanly. I would not discount B005 for lack of commercial reach, since conceptual influence on perovskite cells is real, but I note that this is an argument about influence on a later field rather than about use. For chemistry as a whole, I find the evidence of daily use in B055, in syntheses and industry, easier to document than for a cell that has not reached the market. On Hagfeldt, a third name would weaken the clean two-person attribution that you rely on, so the committee should decide that question first.

uncertainties: Whether five members will accept C-N coupling as distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize, which I judge the decisive question for B055.
Whether Kosugi's precedent should be credited. I hold at two names, but have not independently verified the priority record.

If B055 cannot reach five votes, I would move to B011 with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli and a PROTAC-focused citation, as my first fallback, with B042 next. I would do so as a pragmatic judgement about what the committee can defend and not because I am persuaded that B011 is ahead scientifically.

Whether B011 needs a second part or a wider citation to cover molecular glues, and whether the committee considers an absence of an approved degrader a reason to wait. I have not verified current clinical status for any candidate.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with any shortlisted candidate: none of the names credited for B055, B011 or B042 is a mentor, collaborator or institutional colleague. My Masamune training is in stereocontrolled synthesis, not coupling catalysis. I share Lund University with Linke and Sparr, which I note without treating it as a conflict. As the only synthetic organic chemist on the committee I have a perspective bias towards methodology, which colleagues should weigh when reading my preference for B055.
